newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BROKERS WANT CHANGES TO SHARE SUSPENSIONS.
newsitem.headline: BROKERS WANT CHANGES TO SHARE SUSPENSIONS.

text.p: Lithuanian brokers said on Friday they want share suspensions on the bourse to be cut to a minimun as they weather a wave of suspensions of their favourite shares on what is already a sluggish market.
"These stoppages are limiting the rights of investors to sell or buy stocks," said Romas Matukas, president of the national brokers association, which is pressing for a change in the rules.

"The brokers association has proposed to the securities commission, stock exchange and central depository not to stop trading unless it is technically impossible -- like when the central depository assimilates issues," Matukas said.
"Any other other reasons are not reasonable, like the reorganisation of Lithuanian Energy," Matukas added.
Matukas said he expected the securities commission to decide at the end of June.

Traders recently saw Lithuanian Energy, Vilniaus Bank, Vilniaus Vingis, Liteksas and Calw, Rokishkis Cheese, Sanitas and the Lithuanian Savings Bank suspended for shareholders meetings, assimilations of share issues and other formalities.
Trading in some shares has already resumed and most of the rest are expected to be active in the first week of June, except Lithuanian Energy which will not be back until mid-June.
"For Lithuanian and foreign investors, it's difficult to understand the purpose of these suspensions," said Grazina Bachiuliene, a broker with Vilfima.
Matukas and other critics say the stock exchange rules allow companies to suspend trading voluntarliy.

"If a company asks the stock exchange board to stop trades with its shares, the stock exchange board will automatically stop trade," Matukus said. "The maximum term for stopping trade is up to three months."
"This voluntary approach to trading should be ended," said Kestutis Kupshys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe
"Every company that is listed may request a suspension of trading and those suspensions are normally executed without proper notice," Kupshys said.
An official from the stock exhange said that it is not that easy for companies to suspend trade in their shares.
"A company can request a suspension but it cannot just be for any reason," said Dalia Jasulaityte, director of the trading and settlement department at the stock exchange.
"Companies have to explain the reasons to the board of the stock exchange," Jasulaityte said.
